title: Surface topology and incidence theorems over division rings
summary: Incidence theorems concern configurations of points, lines, and, more generally, higher-dimensional subspaces in projective space. Broadly speaking, such theorems fall into two classes: those that hold over an arbitrary division ring, such as Desargues' theorem, and those that hold only over fields, such as Pappus' theorem. In this paper, we explain the topological origin of this distinction.
